title: Common Free Time Across Schedules
statement: You are given schedules, a list where each element is one employee's schedule. An employee's schedule is a list of disjoint busy intervals [start, end] with start < end, already sorted by start. Return the list of finite intervals of positive length during which every employee is simultaneously free. A moment is free for an employee if it lies in no busy interval of that employee. Report only the gaps that fall between the earliest and latest busy moments across all employees: ignore the unbounded free time before everyone's first busy interval and after everyone's last one. Each returned interval [a, b] must have a < b (zero-length gaps, where one interval ends exactly when the next begins, are excluded). Return the intervals as a list of [start, end] pairs sorted by start; the starts are distinct so this order is unique. If there is no such common free interval, return an empty list.
hints: Every employee is free at a moment only when that moment lies outside every busy interval, so what does the union of all busy intervals across all employees look like?

Flatten all employees' intervals into one list, sort by start, then merge overlaps while tracking a running maximum end; the common free time is exactly the positive-length gaps between merged blocks.

Walk the sorted intervals keeping prev_end as the running max end seen so far. When the next start exceeds prev_end, emit [prev_end, start] and reset prev_end to this interval's end; otherwise extend prev_end with max(prev_end, end). Never compare against only the immediately preceding interval, or a containing block like [1,10] before [2,3],[4,5] fabricates a phantom gap [3,4].
